extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting papers to NeurIPS 2025 (main track, datasets & benchmarks, position papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for preparing and submitting papers (and supplements) to NeurIPS 2025, including formatting, anonymization, deadlines, review process, and ethical/legal policies. Applies to main track and related tracks unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract submission deadline and placeholder abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a mandatory abstract submission deadline on May 11, 2025 AoE; titles and abstracts may be edited until the full paper submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions with "placeholder" abstracts that are rewritten for the full submission risk being removed without consideration. Placeholder examples include titles/abstracts that provide little or no semantic information (e.g., "We provide a new semi-supervised learning method."). After the abstract deadline, adding or removing authors is not allowed, but listed authors can potentially be reordered before the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full paper submission deadline and OpenReview profile requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Full paper submission deadline is May 15, 2025 AoE and all authors must have an OpenReview profile when submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OpenReview profiles must be up to date, with all publications and current affiliations. Submissions without the authors' updated OpenReview profiles will be desk rejected. The information is critical for conflicts-of-interest handling and reviewer matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical appendices and supplementary material deadlines and size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical appendices and supplementary materials deadline: May 22, 2025 AoE (separate from the full paper deadline). Authors may submit technical appendices with the paper or as a separate PDF/ZIP before the supplementary material deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no page limit for technical appendices. Authors may submit up to 100MB of technical appendices and supplementary material. Supplementary material should be created by the authors and directly supports the submission content. Reviewers may choose whether to look at appendices/supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission file format and suggested order
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be in PDF format and a single PDF file. The suggested order is: the submitted paper content, paper references, the NeurIPS paper checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may optionally include some or all technical appendices in the same PDF above, but those included parts cannot be changed after the full submission deadline. The NeurIPS paper checklist forms part of the submission but does not count towards the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main text page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The main text of a submitted paper is limited to nine content pages, including all figures and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional pages containing references, checklist, and optional technical appendices do not count as content pages. If accepted, authors are allowed one additional content page for the camera-ready version. Violating page limits may lead to rejection without further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum file size for main submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum file size for a main paper submission is 50MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical appendices/supplementary material submitted separately can be up to 100MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required use of NeurIPS 2025 LaTeX style
rubrics_metrics.description: You must format your submission using the NeurIPS 2025 LaTeX style file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The style file includes a "preprint" option for non-anonymous preprints. Submissions that violate the NeurIPS style (e.g., by decreasing margins or font sizes) may be rejected without further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to complete a paper checklist as part of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist helps authors reflect on issues relating to responsible ML research, including reproducibility, transparency, research ethics, and societal impact. The checklist is part of the submission and does not count towards the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization and double-blind reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be anonymized and may not contain any identifying information that may violate the double-blind reviewing policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy applies to any supplementary or linked material, including code. If including links to external material, authors are responsible to guarantee anonymous browsing. Do not include acknowledgments at submission time. When citing your own papers, anonymize references (e.g., "In the previous work of Smith et al. [1]…" instead of "In our previous work [1]..."). For citing a concurrently submitted anonymized NeurIPS submission, include the anonymized copy in the supplementary material and write "Anonymous et al. [1] concurrently show..." Any papers found to be violating this policy will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM (Large Language Model) usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The NeurIPS policy for use of Large Language Models (LLMs) applies and authors are responsible for following it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A link to the LLM policy is provided; authors must ensure compliance in content generation, attribution, and anonymity as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and Area Chairs may flag submissions for ethics review; flagged submissions are sent to an ethics review committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments from ethics reviewers are considered by primary reviewers and ACs and are visible to authors who may respond. Ethics reviewers do not have authority to reject papers, but in extreme cases papers may be rejected by program chairs on ethical grounds regardless of scientific quality or contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and non-anonymous prior posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of non-anonymous preprints (e.g., arXiv) will not result in rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using the NeurIPS style for a preprint, use the "preprint" option rather than "final." Reviewers are instructed not to actively look for preprints, and encountering them does not constitute a conflict of interest. Authors may submit anonymized work already available as a preprint without citing it. Public versions should not state "Under review at NeurIPS" or similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions substantially similar to papers previously published or submitted in parallel to other peer-reviewed venues with proceedings or journals may not be submitted to NeurIPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers previously presented at workshops are permitted if they did not appear in conference proceedings, journals, or books. NeurIPS coordinates with other conferences to identify dual submissions. Dual submissions may be desk rejected at any time during reviewing and program building. Slicing contributions too thinly is discouraged. Dual submissions to both the main conference track and the Datasets & Benchmarks track will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-collusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS prohibits collusion whereby authors secretly cooperate with reviewers, Area Chairs, or Senior Area Chairs to obtain favorable reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties include immediate removal from the reviewing system, rejection of all papers under consideration, and/or sanctions to future NeurIPS participation. If collusion is identified, the involved parties will be notified and allowed to respond; PCs will deliberate and their decision is final. Collusion can be identified at any point, including bidding and rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response/rebuttal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have one week to view and respond to initial reviews; responses may not contain identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may not submit revisions of their paper or supplemental material during rebuttal, but may post their responses as a discussion in OpenReview. After the initial response period, authors can respond to further reviewer/AC questions by posting on the submission forum. Program chairs reserve the right to solicit additional reviews after the initial author response period; such additional reviews will be visible to authors and authors will have a chance to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication transparency for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For accepted papers, reviews, meta-reviews, and any discussion with the authors will be made public (reviewer/AC/SAC identities remain anonymous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Camera-ready papers will be due in advance of the conference. All camera-ready papers must include a funding disclosure. Authors are strongly encouraged to submit accompanying code and data when appropriate. Authors will be allowed to make minor changes for a short period after the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option for rejected authors to opt in to public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: After the notification deadline, accepted and opted-in rejected papers will be made public and open for non-anonymous public commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous reviews, meta-reviews, author responses and reviewer responses for those papers will also be made public. Authors of rejected papers will have two weeks after the notification deadline to opt in to make their deanonymized rejected papers public in OpenReview. These opt-in papers are not counted as NeurIPS publications and will be shown as rejected in OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous work and citation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that appeared online after March 1st, 2025 will generally be considered "contemporaneous" and not grounds for rejection; authors must still cite and discuss contemporaneous work as feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any paper that influenced the submission is prior work and must be cited and discussed. Submissions very similar to contemporaneous work will undergo additional scrutiny for plagiarism and missing credit to prior work. Plagiarism is prohibited by the NeurIPS Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track-specific portals and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets & Benchmarks (D&B) submissions should be submitted to a different OpenReview portal; papers will not be transferred between main and D&B after submission is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D&B adheres to main track guidelines for formatting, supplementary materials, LLM use, ethics review, preprints, dual submissions, anti-collusion, author responses, and publication unless the D&B CFP states otherwise. A new Position Paper track is introduced with formatting consistent with the main track and a required "lay summary" for accepted position papers; Position Paper deadlines are slightly later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments on the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Program chairs will measure the quality and effectiveness of the review process via randomized controlled experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All experiments are independently reviewed and approved by an Institutional Review Board (IRB). Program chairs and D&B track chairs will decide whether experiments apply to either or both tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid designation for student authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper may designate up to one NeurIPS.cc account email address of a corresponding student author who confirms they need support to attend and agrees to volunteer if selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered for financial aid the student will also need to fill out the Financial Aid application when it becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile creation/moderation details
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview profiles must be created or updated by the full paper submission deadline; new profiles without institutional email are subject to moderation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New profiles created without an institutional email will go through a moderation process that can take up to two weeks. New profiles created with an institutional email will be activated automatically. Use OpenReview FAQ for help importing publications (DBLP recommended but not required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material provenance and reviewer discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material (data, source code) should be created by the authors and directly supports the submission content; reviewers have discretion whether to view it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to upload code specifically as part of supplementary material to help reviewers assess quality. Check the code submission policy and templates for further details.
